editorial:
Imagine waking up one day and finding out you are suddenly rich because you saved a baron's life. That is exactly what happens to a simple shoemaker in this funny old-school comedy. You will see him go from a humble worker to a guy who thinks he is better than everyone else. He starts acting like a royal, pushing away his best friends and even telling his own daughter that her boyfriend, a carpenter, is not good enough for their new social status. It is a classic story about how money can change a person for the worse, but it keeps things light and silly throughout.

You will love how the main character gets tricked by fake fancy people who just want his money. The acting is over-the-top in a way that makes the jokes land well, though the pacing feels a bit slower than modern films. If you like vintage comedies that teach a lesson about being humble, you should definitely give this a try. Since it is an older film, your best bet is to look for a remastered version.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the shoemaker realizes the fancy people he trusted were just lying to steal his wealth. He loses his money and his pride, which forces him to apologize to the friends and family he treated badly. In the end, he finds happiness by returning to his roots. His daughter gets to be with the carpenter, and the shoemaker learns that being a good person is worth more than any inheritance.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic comedies about rich and poor people.
